```{r message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(1)
```

## Problem 1

```{r}
birthdays = function(n) {
  
  days = sample(x = 1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)
  
  anyDuplicated(days) > 0
  
}
```

```{r}
bday_results_df = 
  expand_grid(
    sample_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    shared_bdays = map_lgl(sample_size, birthdays)
  )
```

```{r}
bday_prob_df = 
bday_results_df |> 
  group_by(sample_size) |> 
  summarize(
    shared_prob = mean(shared_bdays)
    ) 
```

```{r}
bday_prob_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = sample_size, y = shared_prob)) + 
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of Birthday Repeats by Sample Size", 
    x = "Sample Size",
    y = "Probability of Shared Birthday") 
```

There is a very low probability of shared birthdays when pulling a two person sample, and near 1 probability when pulling from a sample of 50. I was honestly suprised by this result -- I didn't expect the probability to be almost 100% at such a low sample size. The curve generally follows an S shape, with the largest slope in the middle range of the sample sizes.

## Problem 3

```{r}
sim_mean_sd = function(n, mu = 0, sigma = 5) {
  
  sim_data = tibble(
    x = rnorm(n, mean = mu, sd = sigma),
  )
  
  sim_data |> 
    summarize(
      mu_hat = mean(x),
      sigma_hat = sd(x)
    )
}
```

```{r}
output = vector("list", 5000)

for (i in 1:5000) {
  output[[i]] = sim_mean_sd(30)
}

sim_results = bind_rows(output)
```

```{r}
sim_results_df = 
  expand_grid(
    sample_size = 30,
    iter = 1:5000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    estimate_df = map(sample_size, sim_mean_sd)
  ) |> 
  unnest(estimate_df)
```
